mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% signals economic weakness, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS show positive month-over-month growth.

mechanism_narrative: In the industrial expansion phase (INDPRO > 102), rising manufacturing output supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 102.

mechanism_narrative: Higher retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of observations with RSAFS above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% per annum signals potential monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer confidence and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS grows and UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: During housing market recovery (HOUST > 900 thousand units), increased residential construction activity signals economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 900 thousand units.
